scope: All units read: text for sense, translation and word glosses against the text. The text was not compared with the source page.

items.issue: āmīlitākṣam describes Mukunda, whom the glance has reached; the translation gave the half-closed eyes to Lakṣmī and attached “unwinking, ruled by love” to Mukunda.
items.change: Retranslated: his eyes half-closed; her eye unwinking, ruled by love.

items.issue: dhārādhare is the standard of comparison (lightning on a rain-cloud), not an epithet “the rain-bearer”.
items.change: Now “… lovely as a bank of dark clouds, she flashes like lightning upon a rain-cloud”.

items.issue: “golden pitchers at the mouths of the elephants” misplaced mukha: the water pours from the mouths of the pitchers.
items.change: Now “poured by the elephants of the quarters from the mouths of golden pitchers”.

items.issue: hārāvalī was glossed “a string of pearls” beside “made of sapphire”.
The gloss of iṣṭāviśiṣṭamatayaḥ contradicted the translation (“even the undistinguished”).
items.change: Gloss aligned, with a note that the compound is read in more than one way.

items.issue: The page reads duṣkarmadharmam apanīya. The usual text is duṣkarmagharmam, “the heat of ill deeds”, which is what a rain-cloud removes; dharmam looks like a misprint of gha as dha. The translation (“burden of ill deeds”) covers neither exactly.
options: A. Emend to duṣkarmagharmam, translate “the scorching heat of ill deeds”, and log it.
B. Keep dharmam and the present translation.
items.recommend: A: the image requires it and it is the common reading.

items.issue: iṣṭāviśiṣṭamatayo'pi: the translation takes it as “even the undistinguished”. Others divide iṣṭā viśiṣṭamatayaḥ (“the dear, the discerning”) or take iṣṭa as sacrifices (“those intent only on rites”).
options: B. “even those whose minds go no further than their rites”.
items.recommend: A: with api (“even”) it gives the best sense.
